purpose: Prospectively time the three unseen Rust programs using fixed coefficients chosen retrospectively on the separate 15-case study. Compare collection CPU for full-feature and recurrence-only diagnostics on those same binaries.
order: Rotate the canonical programs left by the offset once per round. Each quadruplet brackets a full and a recurrence-only observation with native controls. The full probe runs first if the zero-based round number plus the canonical program index is even.
platform: A second disposable Seoul N2D VM, one thread per core, measured on guest CPU 1, observer and normal guest services on CPU 0. Use the same image, compiler and ordinary/feature clients as the training study. Keep hard cpuset and independently verify each measured PID and loader exec. Retain all outputs and exact ELFs.
measure: Compile each frozen source once with the unchanged Rust 1.95 optimized flags. Use the same binary and input in every mode. Select full feature mode or -loop_recurrence_only in the same existing DSO. Co-load the production v10 client with x86-64-v2 and take the ordinary instructions from its uninterrupted one-process, one-thread receipt. Full additionally requires instruction equality with the independent feature counter. Check all four phase outputs and times, without removing any slow observation.
analysis: For each family use its six-native median as the target and require all three frozen predictions to fall within ±20% to pass. Report each family including native floor and spread, score fast and full separately, and compare them pairwise by abs(fast_prediction-full_prediction)/full_prediction <= 0.001. Report median paired fast/full child CPU ratio by program, mode order, and pooled CPU. Do not refit. This three-family experiment qualifies only its named cases.
